entries.title: Israel seizes castle in Lebanon as it expands ground offensive
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu calls the capture of the strategic fortress a "decisive shift" in Israel's campaign against Hezbollah, as European governments criticise the escalation.

entries.title: Colombia presidential runoff pits leftist senator against pro-Trump rival
entries.snippet: Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda will face Trump admirer Abelardo de la Espriella at the final ballot on 21 June.

entries.title: Trump seeking edits to US-Iran deal, US media report
entries.snippet: The requested changes are related to the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium, according to US media.

entries.title: Japan defence minister denies militarism and criticises China's 'huge arsenal'
entries.snippet: Shinjiro Koizumi makes some of Tokyo's most pointed remarks yet in the dispute over Japan's military build-up.

entries.title: Huge blast kills dozens in rebel-held village in Myanmar
entries.snippet: Insurgents say it was caused by explosives being used for mining close to the Chinese border.

entries.title: Hundreds arrested and dozens of police injured after Champions League riots in France
entries.snippet: Nearly 800 people were arrested after clashes with police which saw 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

entries.title: South Africa made to look like fools over World Cup visa issues, says minister
entries.snippet: After a day of uncertainty, the government confirms the team will depart for Mexico on Monday.

entries.title: Dead whale towed ashore in Denmark ahead of autopsy
entries.snippet: "Timmy" was found dead off the coast of Anholt despite multiple attempts to rescue it.

entries.title: Nicaraguan indigenous leader dies after three years in prison
entries.snippet: Rights groups condemn the death of Brooklyn Rivera, 73, following his long arbitrary detention by the governing regime.

entries.title: Laos cave survivors help with plan to find last two missing men
entries.snippet: So far, five men have been freed from the narrow, flooded cave but efforts are ongoing to locate two more.

entries.title: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection
entries.snippet: If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa, since the outbreak began in DR Congo.

entries.title: 'Cancel it', Trump says after artists drop out of US Freedom 250 festival
entries.snippet: Trump suggests holding a "Make America Great Again" rally instead after most headliners drop out of White-House-linked event.

entries.title: Nigerian retired general abducted with his wife in the north-west
entries.snippet: Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar's kidnapping highlights continuing security challenges facing parts of the country.

entries.title: Oscar-winning Star Wars editor Marcia Lucas dies aged 80
entries.snippet: The film editor and ex-wife of director George Lucas was widely recognised as a pivotal creative force behind the original space trilogy.

entries.title: Italy bans Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts over security concerns
entries.snippet: Local authorities say the cancellation of other West concerts had played a role in the decision.

entries.title: Ebola spread in DR Congo 'deeply alarming', MSF warns
entries.snippet: The medical charity's comments come as the head of the World Health Organization visits the region worst-hit by the virus outbreak.

entries.title: US, UK and Australia to develop underwater drone technology
entries.snippet: The technology, developed under the Aukus military pact, is aimed at protecting undersea cables and boosting naval defence.

entries.title: Trump attacks artists dropping out of US Freedom 250 concert and mulls appearing himself
entries.snippet: Performers Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride raised concerns the event will be political.

entries.title: Four more men freed from flooded Laos cave after 10 days
entries.snippet: Two of the seven villagers who entered the narrow tunnels in search for gold on 20 May are still missing.

entries.title: A year of grief and waiting: What remains when a plane falls from the sky
entries.snippet: A year after the Air India crash, a mother still speaks about her dead son in the present tense and a brother waits for answers.

entries.title: How aid cuts are hampering the frontline response to the Ebola crisis
entries.snippet: Aid workers in Uganda are watching the Ebola crisis unfold in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. They're doing what they can to prepare for an uptick in cases, but foreign aid cuts aren't helping.

entries.title: The terrifying day the U.S.-Iran war reached a sleepy Sri Lankan town
entries.snippet: A deadly strike during the first days of the Iran war hit far away in the Indian Ocean, jolting a quiet seaside town and showing how far the conflict's reach extends.

entries.title: Trump floats MAGA rally instead of concert after musicians drop out of Freedom 250
entries.snippet: Several artists, including country singer Martina McBride, have withdrawn from the Great American State Fair in Washington, D.C.

entries.title: United Airlines flight to Spain pulls U-turn, apparently over Bluetooth device name
entries.snippet: The flight to Palma de Mallorca diverted back to Newark late on Saturday. Air traffic audio and social media posts indicate an onboard Bluetooth device raised security concerns.

entries.title: U.S. strike on alleged drug boat kills 3 in Pacific Ocean, in fourth attack this week
entries.snippet: The U.S. military said it carried out another strike on a boat accused of smuggling drugs in the Pacific Ocean, killing three in the fourth attack this week and putting the total death toll at 205.

entries.title: Israel seizes medieval castle as it expands major offensive in southern Lebanon
entries.snippet: Israel has captured the 12th-century Beaufort castle that overlooks southern Lebanon and northern Israel. The move suggests Israel is planning an extended military presence in Lebanon.

entries.title: Experimental pill promises new hope for deadly pancreatic cancer
entries.snippet: A novel pill helped people with advanced pancreatic cancer live longer, researchers reported Sunday, raising hopes of long-needed better treatments for one of the deadliest types of cancer.

entries.title: Israel is extending its footprint through war. For some, it's part of a greater plan
entries.snippet: On the fringes of Israel's far right, some activists and political leaders dream of a Greater Israel, extending the country's area of control into neighboring countries.

entries.title: The biggest permanent desert lake threatens with rising waters and hungry crocs
entries.snippet: Kenya's Lake Turkana is the world's largest permanent desert lake. Its waters have long sustained hundreds of thousands. Now the lake is facing multiple threats — and threatening those who rely on it.

entries.title: Democrats and Republicans think control of Congress runs through Iowa
entries.snippet: Iowa is no stranger to political attention in presidential elections, but surprisingly competitive midterm contests highlight the state's importance for both parties as it holds its primary Tuesday.

entries.title: Polls close in Colombia vote with Espriella and Cepeda advancing to runoff
entries.snippet: Lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella and peace-builder Iván Cepeda were leading the vote counts in the first round of Colombia's presidential elections on Sunday, and are to face off in a presidential runoff in the South American nation later in June.

entries.title: Platner's wife calls reports about Senate candidate's explicit texts with women 'shameful'
entries.snippet: Graham Platner's wife called reports that her husband had previously exchanged sexually explicit text messages with several women "shameful" over the weekend, the latest controversy to hit the Maine Democrat's whirlwind campaign.

entries.title: Older Americans often compelled to keep working — and face criticism for doing so
entries.snippet: Over the past several decades, demographic and economic changes have significantly altered how people experience work and aging.

entries.title: Indigenous rights leader Brooklyn Rivera dies after nearly 3 years detained in Nicaragua
entries.snippet: Brooklyn Rivera, a renowned Indigenous leader from Nicaragua who spent years fighting for the rights of his community and was imprisoned by the government in September 2023, has died.

entries.title: Farmers seek fertilizer alternatives as Iran war drives up prices
entries.snippet: Since the Iran war began on Feb. 28, fertilizer prices have risen by 40%.

entries.title: Experimental drug shows promise against deadly pancreatic cancer
entries.snippet: A novel pill helped people with advanced pancreatic cancer live longer, researchers reported Sunday, raising hopes of long-needed better treatments for one of the deadliest types of cancer.

entries.title: Recovering wetlands fuel growth of flamingo population in Venice
entries.snippet: The pale pink birds — called "fenicotteri" in Italian — are now flocking to Venice in record numbers, as ecological efforts to restore damaged wetlands could help expand their habitat and possibly induce them to nest in the lagoon.

entries.title: WHO chief reports 5 Ebola recoveries as new treatment center opens in Congo
entries.snippet: Five patients have recovered from a rare type of Ebola virus, the head of the World Health Organization said Sunday during a visit to Bunia in eastern Congo.

entries.title: Hundreds detained in France after violence erupts following Paris Saint-Germain victory
entries.snippet: A huge crowd of supporters gathered peacefully near the Eiffel Tower on Sunday to celebrate Paris Saint-Germain's second Champions League title victory, which was marred by violent clashes overnight across France and led police to detain hundreds of people.

entries.title: Israeli troops seize strategic castle in Lebanon during deepest incursion in decades
entries.snippet: Israeli troops have captured a strategic mountain topped with a Crusader-built castle in southern Lebanon in the deepest incursion into the country in more than a quarter-century, the military said Sunday.

entries.title: Do you need SPF 30, 50 or 100? Dermatologists answer your burning sunscreen questions
entries.snippet: PolitiFact asked board-certified dermatologists to answer people's burning questions about SPF. When it comes to sunscreen, they advised buying broad-spectrum sunscreen that's SPF 30 or higher and reapplying regularly.

entries.title: Trump plans to appeal ruling letting importers seek refunds of paid struck-down tariffs
entries.snippet: Businesses big and small have started receiving tariff refunds after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that President Trump lacked the constitutional authority to impose higher import taxes on goods from nearly every other country.

entries.title: Fact-checking Trump on National Mall's Reflecting Pool renovations
entries.snippet: As President Donald Trump delves into several projects to remake the monumental core of the nation's capital, PolitiFact fact-checks statements he's made about renovations he's ordered for the National Mall's Reflecting Pool.

entries.title: Bus driver charged after Virginia crash kills 5, including family headed to wedding
entries.snippet: A family of four from Massachusetts who were killed when a bus crashed into multiple vehicles in Virginia were traveling to a wedding with a carload of homemade desserts for the celebration.

entries.title: Colombia accuses Ecuador of interfering in its general election
entries.snippet: Colombia's government rejected a move by Ecuador's president to eliminate tariffs on Colombian imports because of a tariff commitment made to an opposition candidate, calling it "deliberate interference" in the ongoing electoral process.

entries.title: U.S. says it stopped a merchant ship trying to breach blockade and reach Iran
entries.snippet: The U.S. military stopped a merchant vessel trying to break through its blockade of Iranian ports by firing a missile into its engine room, the U.S. Central Command said on Saturday.

entries.title: Four men rescued from flooded Laos cave as search continues for 2 others
entries.snippet: Rescue workers in Laos said Saturday they have safely evacuated four villagers trapped in a flooded cave for 10 days.

entries.title: Autopsy planned for dead humpback whale brought ashore in Denmark
entries.snippet: The carcass of a humpback whale, whose life and death captivated Germans for months as the mammal became repeatedly stranded in the Baltic Sea, was dragged Saturday onto a Danish beach.

entries.title: Thousands flock to Vilnius for festival celebrating Lithuania's iconic cold beet soup
entries.snippet: A festival honoring Lithuania's iconic cold beet soup brought tens of thousands of visitors Saturday to its capital city, which was fully decked out in pink.

entries.title: WHO chief visits Congo Ebola epicenter as cases outpace response
entries.snippet: The head of the WHO on Saturday visited eastern Congo's Bunia, a city at the heart of an outbreak of a rare type of Ebola, where the virus is spreading faster than the response despite better-organized health facilities and new aid arrivals.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany news: Most expect AfD state premier after elections
entries.snippet: Most people in Germany expect a premier from the far-right AfD to lead at least one state after elections in the autumn, a survey has found. The Brenner Pass linking Austria and Italy has reopened.

entries.title: New York: Mayor Mamdani skips annual Israel Day Parade
entries.snippet: In a break from decades of political tradition, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the annual parade celebrating Israel.

entries.title: Germany’s thriving Alevi community
entries.snippet: The Alevis make up the fourth largest religious community in Germany today. What are the main tenets of their faith? And how are they preserving their unique culture?

entries.title: Shangri-La conference: Asia-Pacific on path to rearmament
entries.snippet: Military budgets are rising worldwide. At the security conference in Singapore, the focus was also on achieving greater security through more weapons — as the growing rivalry between the US and China dominated talks.

entries.title: Myanmar: Dozens dead in explosives storage blast in rebel-controlled area
entries.snippet: An explosion in northeastern Myanmar killed dozens of people in an area controlled by rebels. Preliminary reports suggest that the blast occurred at a site where large quantities of mining explosives were stored.

entries.title: Space race: Why Portugal is reaching for the stars
entries.snippet: A spaceport is being built on a small Portuguese island in the Atlantic. Is Portugal on the verge of becoming a space nation?

entries.title: Middle East: Israel captures key fortress amid Lebanon push
entries.snippet: Israeli troops have captured the strategically important Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon after heavy clashes with Hezbollah. Meanwhile, Trump has toughened the terms for a deal to end the war with Iran. DW has more.

entries.title: Malta's Labour Party wins historic fourth term: preliminary results
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Robert Abela, who campaigned on the strength of the economy, had been widely expected to win the vote.

entries.title: Japan and China trade accusations at Shangri-La Dialogue
entries.snippet: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has strongly rejected China's claim that Japan is moving toward “neo-militarism.” He accused Beijing of rapidly arming itself.

entries.title: Brazil is set to cut in on China's rare earths dominance
entries.snippet: Brazil is seeing increasing demand for its vast reserves of rare earth elements. Global mining giants are betting on Brazil as the next powerhouse for critical magnetic metals and an alternative to China's dominance.

entries.title: Swing Youth: In Nazi Germany, jazz was an act of defiance
entries.snippet: The Nazis denounced jazz music as "degenerate art," despite its widespread popularity in Germany. As the Nazis clamped down on expression, groups of jazz-loving teenagers formed the Swing Youth to rebel.

entries.title: India news: BrahMos missile deal signed with Vietnam
entries.snippet: India's defense secretary says a deal has been signed to ‌supply Vietnam with BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles. Meanwhile, retail inflation could hit Indians hard soon. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Goodbye, Norma Jeane: How Marilyn Monroe changed Hollywood
entries.snippet: Long seen primarily as a sex symbol, Marilyn Monroe is now viewed as an early advocate for women in Hollywood. On the 100th anniversary of her birth, DW looks at the star who balanced fame and feminist agency.

entries.title: Meteor explodes over United States, triggering sonic boom
entries.snippet: A meteor broke apart over the US state of Massachusetts. Several people reported that the buildings they were in shook during the incident.

entries.title: Ukraine: IAEA seeks access to Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant after reported drone strike
entries.snippet: Russia claims that a Ukrainian drone struck the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. Ukraine has denied the accusation. The International Atomic Energy Agency has sought to examine the facility.

entries.title: Venezuela opposition candidate Gonzalez urges new elections
entries.snippet: Venezuelan former opposition candidate Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia called for fresh presidential elections in Venezuela. The push comes around five months after US forces captured former President Nicolas Maduro.

entries.title: Trump says he'll replace artists who backed out of concert with himself
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump called the artists who canceled on the 250th anniversary event "third rate," and said he would headline the event himself.

entries.title: France: Police detain many after PSG Champions League win
entries.snippet: Soccer fans flooded the famed Champs-Elysees and riots took place in the French capital after Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League final.

entries.title: PSG's team of talents retain Champions League title
entries.snippet: Paris Saint-Germain were unable to score from open play against a resilient Arsenal but won their second successive title on penalties. Luis Enrique has built a team to be proud of at the oil-rich club.
